finding: DEC-2's least-privilege rationale does not hold for the data actually revealed: the endpoint returns the CALLER'S OWN tool_use.input, and the handler concedes that value already reaches the same user on every page load.
why: A reader trusting the docs believes raw arguments are CONTAINED when the gate is surface-only.
status: fixed: DEC-2 amended to the constant that ships and the scope restated as a surface gate, not a wire gate.

finding: ITEM-16 opened the built-in Calls tab without opening any edit affordance: isEditable still gates enable/test/edit/delete, the new button is gated on McpServersRead, and drawer history mode forces canManage=false.
status: verified, no change needed.

finding: Default delegation resolved to mcp's tool CARD, which printed tool_use.input UNREDACTED. ~15 of ~20 contributions take that path, so the families most likely to carry a credential bypassed redaction entirely.
why: ITEM-17/DEC-1's stated goal was not met; redactArgs was effectively dead on the delegated path.
status: fixed: redaction moved into a CORE default body (RailStepDetail) every contribution lands on, plus redactedJson applied inside McpToolUseRenderer/McpToolCallUI at source.

finding: #[derive(Debug)] on McpToolCallReveal, whose arguments_json is by construction the unredacted value (guidelines §3).
why: Any future tracing::debug!(?reveal)/panic reprints the credential into the log stream.
status: fixed: hand-written Debug that redacts the field.

finding: The depth bound returned the subtree UNCHANGED, so a deeply nested secret rendered in plaintext while the stored row was redacted.
why: Silent divergence exactly where the file claims to be a mirror.
status: fixed: the bound now returns REDACTED — a redactor may lose detail, never redaction.

finding: The docstring claimed results were redacted; only arguments were.
why: Comment asserting the opposite of the code is how a gap survives review.
status: fixed: the core body's docstring states exactly what it does.

finding: Rust and TS denylists mechanically diffed: 22 keys each, zero divergence; exact + case-insensitive matching preserved; nested objects and arrays walked on the real path.
status: verified.

finding: OpenAPI had not been regenerated for either binary; tsc failed with 6 errors and the reveal endpoint had no dispatch entry, so the panel would have silently queried the caller's most-recent call across ALL conversations.
why: Wrong-data surface rather than a visible failure; branch could not build.
status: fixed: just openapi-regen ran for both binaries; types_ts_parity + types_ts_parity_desktop green; tsc clean in both workspaces.

finding: always_reprompt is required while the client types it optional and writes `?? undefined`.
why: Latent mismatch if the field is ever made conditional; not a break today.
status: open — accepted: the three timing fields are optional and the boolean is always emitted, so an un-reloaded client is unaffected.

finding: The step CONSUMED the paired tool_result but delegation rendered only the ANCHOR, so file's catch-all tool_result renderer never ran — every tool-produced chart/PDF/CSV lost its inline FileCard.
why: Direct INV-2 regression, unguarded by any test; confirmed independently by two auditors.
status: fixed: delegation renders the whole consumed span.

finding: resultBlockFor scanned past tool_use while toolStepSpan stopped at the first non-tool_result, so a step could read status/artifacts from a block it did not consume.
why: Duplicate rows with double-attributed artifacts on raw (un-normalized) parallel calls.
status: fixed: the two now stop at the same place.

finding: A repeated tool_use.id produced duplicate step keys, colliding on the React key, the per-message expansion state and the panel tab id.
why: Expanding one row expanded the other; both opened the same tab.
status: fixed: segmentation disambiguates the second and later sighting.

finding: Three e2e specs still drove the deleted group card's testids; one asserted toHaveCount(0) and would have passed vacuously.
why: Suite red, or false-green for a behaviour that no longer exists.
status: fixed: the three specs are deleted; their invariants are re-covered by the activity-rail specs.

finding: raw/revealError were never reset on tool_use_id change, and the panel host reuses the memoised instance across tabs.
why: Call A's revealed unredacted arguments rendered under call B's record, unaudited.
status: fixed: both reset in the id-keyed effect.

finding: Adversarially scripted: sum(step.consumed) == span.consumed and exactly-once block coverage hold for empty messages, orphan results, result-before-use, id-less tool_use, two results per use and text-interleaved runs; consumed 0/NaN/negative/huge all clamp.
status: verified by the auditor's throwaway scripts.

finding: Descriptors were computed in a memo'd, unsubscribed parent while only the child subscribed, so a call that finished without adding a block stayed 'running' and its 1 Hz timer never cleared.
why: Permanently ticking phantom steps; INV-4's live narration wrong.
status: fixed: descriptors are re-derived in the component that holds the subscription.

finding: Registration happened in an extension's initialize with no matching clear on unregister.
why: A disposed extension kept feeding live statuses and leaked a store subscription.
status: fixed: owner-scoped clearRailLiveSourceIfOwnedBy, called by the registry on unregister.

finding: The live seam is a single process-global counter fed by a whole-store subscribe, so any composer mutation re-renders every mounted rail.
why: Fan-out cost on long agentic conversations.
status: open — accepted for now: correctness is restored; narrowing the seam to per-tool_use_id is a follow-up, recorded in FIX_ROUND-1.

finding: unwrap_or_default() swallowed a DB error into 'no override' (guidelines §6).
why: A transient DB error re-created the misleading 'Approve for this conversation' affordance ITEM-25 removes.
status: fixed: the error is logged at error! before degrading, and the degradation is justified in place.

finding: Clipboard write had no catch (unhandled rejection = a gating runtime-health finding), the reset timeout was never cleared, and reveal had no in-flight guard.
why: No feedback on a failed copy; N audit lines per user intent.
status: fixed: try/catch with visible failure state, cleanup on unmount, and a loading-guarded reveal.

finding: The byte-slice truncation that would panic on a multibyte boundary is genuinely fixed and covered by three regression tests.
status: verified: all three pass.

finding: A blocking descriptor could claim consumed > 1 while the breakout rendered exactly one block.
why: The same span-says-N-renders-M class ITEM-5 claims to have removed.
status: fixed: blocking is pinned to consumed 1 at segmentation.

finding: The AP-4 move created a lateral js-tool -> mcp dependency on an internal store path (guidelines §9).
why: The coupling was inverted in direction, not eliminated.
status: open — recorded: the elicitation transport is genuinely shared; extracting it to a chat/core seam is a follow-up.

finding: Rules of Hooks: every hook precedes the early return in both ActivityRail and RailStep; scoped selectors read only their own key.
status: verified; lint:hooks green.

finding: A FORCED-OPEN (failed) rail rendered its summary as a disabled Button: 50% opacity, unfocusable, tooltip inert.
why: INV-5 exists to make a failure loud; this made it the quietest element in the message.
status: fixed: the non-toggleable state is a status row, not a disabled control.

finding: The step LABEL sat inside a Button disabled whenever the body was empty — which is exactly the in-flight case.
why: Running steps rendered dimmed, unfocusable, with no tooltip for a truncated label.
status: fixed: the label is plain content; only the chevron is a control.

finding: Artifact chips were inert spans with a file icon and a file name.
why: The row advertised files reachable by neither mouse nor keyboard.
status: fixed: chips and the +N overflow are Buttons that open the step body, where the extension's own file view lives.

finding: aria-expanded without aria-controls; the summary's accessible name buried the status mid-string.
why: A screen-reader user got state but no association, and heard 'Activity:' before the failure.
status: fixed: ids + aria-controls on both disclosures; the summary name leads with the status label.

finding: start-[7px] is an off-grid arbitrary spacing value (DESIGN_SYSTEM § Spacing rhythm).
why: A hand-tuned magic offset that silently misaligns if the icon box changes.
status: open — recorded in FIX_ROUND-1.

finding: INV-1 soft violation: core special-cased two scheduler structured-content keys.
why: The invariant forbids special-casing an extension, not merely importing one.
status: fixed: moved into the scheduler contribution (order 20, so still one decision point); core's test now asserts the absence.

finding: INV-6 at risk: the excluded-type set guarded only the ANCHOR, so a consumed range could swallow a text answer block.
why: The guard did not cover the failure mode it names.
status: fixed: the span is clamped at the first excluded block.

finding: INV-2: the MCP server attribution the retired card showed beside every tool name was gone from the transcript.
why: With ~13 built-in servers, 'which server ran this' became unreadable.
status: fixed: serverId is carried on the descriptor.

finding: INV-7 at risk: the delegated cards kept their disclosure in component state.
why: Inside a virtualised list the inner disclosure silently re-collapses on scroll — the ThinkingContent failure, one level deeper.
status: fixed as a side effect: the core detail body has no nested disclosure at all.

finding: Ordinals 25.10-25.14 are DECIMALS: 25.10 == 25.1, colliding with an existing turn.
why: Transcripts order by created_at, so the showcase conversation rendered scrambled — the fixture the design-critic pass reviews.
status: fixed: renumbered to 25.61-25.68, verified strictly increasing and collision-free file-wide, plus a regression test.

finding: The partial indexes omit user_id while every query leads with it, and the ($n IS NULL OR col = $n) shape is not sargable under a generic plan.
why: The index may not be used at all on the interactive panel path.
status: open — recorded: needs an EXPLAIN-backed follow-up; composite (user_id, col) is the likely fix.

finding: The guarded gallery fixture conversation grew by 8 turns.
why: Recorded cassettes could drift.
status: verified: gallery:check-fixtures PASSES after the change.

finding: The new filters AND-narrow into an unconditional user_id = $1 in both the page and COUNT queries; the reveal re-derives ownership through conversations rather than trusting the resolved row.
status: verified by two auditors plus green unit tests.

finding: JsToolApprovalContent moved but the coverage map still keyed the old path; three generated registries were stale.
why: Three sub-checks of npm run check were red.
status: fixed: path re-pointed, all registries regenerated, every check:* script PASSES.

finding: ClaimingContentRenderer has no consumer (as its predecessor did not).
why: Guidelines §15.
status: open — recorded: pre-existing shape, not introduced here.

finding: Every new chat-extension file is reached by the auto-discovery glob, including the module that ships no module.tsx.
status: verified.

finding: TESTS.md claimed TEST-24/TEST-31 coverage for the mcp, workflow and js-tool contributions; none existed.
why: The generic fallback every unclaimed tool lands on was untested, including the decline clause that keeps first-wins honest.
status: fixed: three specs added (17 assertions); js-tool's contributions lifted into a JSX-free module so the runner can reach them.

finding: INV-1's sole guard walked one of the rail's four directories and matched only aliased imports.
why: The invariant could be violated one directory over, or with a relative specifier.
status: fixed: all four directories plus railRegistryCore, relative specifiers resolved, and the scheduler marker keys added to the name scan.

finding: TEST-14 was re-pointed from a .tsx render spec to a pure-helper spec without weakening its enumerated claim.
why: The row primitive has no render-level unit coverage.
status: open — recorded in DRIFT-1.11: the rendering half is asserted in a browser by TEST-8/TEST-2; the enumeration wording still overstates the unit spec.

finding: An [acceptance] proof of INV-3 is built on page.route() SSE mocking (guidelines §14).
why: The invariant is proven against a fabricated stream, not the real approval path.
status: open — recorded: the mocked routes DO exist in openapi.json so there is no stale-mock false-green, but a non-mocked companion is owed.

finding: TEST-34 validates the fixture JSON but never links it to the contribution.
why: A BIOMCP_VERSION bump landing new names leaves both sides green while every new tool degrades.
status: open — recorded in FIX_ROUND-1.

finding: The reveal audit test was reported as having contradictory assertions; the shipped version guards on FIELD names, not the prose.
status: verified: the test runs and passes.

finding: Skip audit across the whole change: exactly one skip exists, a conditional real-LLM env gate. No #[ignore], no unconditional skip.
status: verified — allowed by the house rule.

finding: The new module hosts three homeless built-ins; centralization shrank from nine modules to three rather than being eliminated, with nothing bounding regrowth.
why: A shrunk central map under a new name.
status: open — recorded: accepted as the least-bad owner (the three have no frontend module), with the bound owed.

finding: 17 modules deep-import the rail contract from inside chat's components directory rather than a public barrel (guidelines §9).
why: Any reorganisation of chat/components is a 17-file break.
status: open — recorded in FIX_ROUND-1.

finding: code_sandbox was the one key of the deleted nine-module map with no claimant.
why: Silent coverage loss in a map-to-registry migration.
status: fixed: claimed by the code-sandbox contribution.

finding: Dependency graph re-derived: the rail imports only api-client, lib, kit and other chat modules — no feature module by static, dynamic, type-only or string-literal reference. The nine-module map is genuinely deleted and not recreated in railBlocks.
status: verified by two auditors plus the widened isolation test.

finding: segmentRail runs unmemoized per render and each declining contribution re-ran several forward scans; a streaming turn re-renders per token.
why: Quadratic-ish work over a turn versus the single scan the old path did.
status: fixed: railToolStepBase is memoized per (blocks identity, index) with a live-version epoch, so a declining contribution costs a lookup.

finding: renderStepDetail is evaluated eagerly for every step including collapsed ones, re-running registry resolution.
why: Doubles resolution cost per visible step per render.
status: open — recorded: mitigated by the base memo above; a lazy thunk is the remaining fix.

finding: An extra DB round trip per approval frame for data the gate already had.
why: Redundant query on an interactive path.
status: open — recorded; approvals are user-paced.

finding: The deep link is built from window.location, which inside a Tauri webview is tauri://localhost.
why: On desktop the copy-link affordance yields a link nobody can open.
status: open — recorded in FIX_ROUND-1: needs the configured public origin, or hiding under __TAURI__.

finding: toLocaleString with no explicit locale.
why: Output differs by host locale, making assertions locale-sensitive across the three build hosts.
status: open — recorded.

finding: The desktop workspace overlays ui/src and holds no stale copy of any touched chat file; both OpenAPI twins regenerated together.
status: verified: desktop tsc exits 0 and types_ts_parity_desktop passes.
